about: Polyphony heard: how many voices a listener follows at once. Read by counterpoint (public/shared/conducting/counterpoint.js), which keeps a line's rules against the voices heard with it. A limit of hearing, not of composing: the owner, 5 November 2026: "listeners' difficulty in DISTINGUISHING three voices does not invalidate COMPOSING many more voices, since sometimes compositions use excesses beyond distinction to generate nuanced differences in texture".

voices-followed.where: the abstract and its experiments, as summarized (the full text not saved: research/SOURCES_TO_FETCH.md)
voices-followed.conditions: musicians judging how many voices sound, and when one enters, in polyphony of homogeneous timbre (Bach)
voices-followed.note: the voices a listener counts and follows: errors from about one in ten with three voices to about one in two with four. Past it a texture's voices are heard as the texture, not each -- which a composition may want (micropolyphony: counterpoint.js)
